# Appendix A: Environment Setup {#sec-appendix-a .unnumbered}

[Part 0](../chapters/chapter_00.qmd) covers everything you need to
install Python, create a virtual environment, check your hardware, and
run the book's chapter scripts — start there if you haven't already.
This appendix covers a few things Part 0 doesn't: the training dataset's
layout, rendering this book itself (not just running its code), a
data-handling note for your own reports, and troubleshooting for a few
less common errors.

If you'd like a guide specific to the editor or notebook environment you
chose in Part 0, see Appendices A1–A5 instead.

## 1. The training dataset

Chapters 1–5 use ten real, curated Daily Drilling and completion reports
from the public Utah FORGE archive (well FORGE 16A(78)-32) — already
committed as PDFs in `datasets/sample_training_set/`, the same
curated subset used in the author's previous book. Part II's "at scale"
chapters use the full 76-report archive, committed at
`datasets/full_training_set/`. Nothing needs to be generated or
downloaded to start: cloning the repository (Part 0) gives you the full
dataset. See `book/datasets/README.md` for the full policy and license
note.

If you want to reproduce the curated subset from the full archive, or
extend it with more reports, see
`code/chapter_01/build_sample_training_set.py`.

## 2. Rendering the book with Quarto

Running the chapter scripts (Part 0) doesn't require anything beyond
Python. Rebuilding this book itself — the HTML and PDF you're reading —
is a separate step that needs [Quarto](https://quarto.org) 1.7 or later:

```bash
quarto --version
```

If that's not recognised, install Quarto from
[quarto.org](https://quarto.org) for your operating system.

With Quarto installed and your virtual environment active:

```bash
quarto render
```

Output is written to `_book/`. For live-editing a single chapter while
you write:

```bash
quarto preview chapters/chapter_01.qmd
```

Or, if you prefer conda/mamba instead of the `.venv` approach from Part 0:

```bash
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate llm-ft-drilling-completions-book
```

## 3. Hardware notes

Fine-tuning, even parameter-efficiently, is more hardware-sensitive than
retrieval:

- **GPU (NVIDIA/CUDA or Apple Silicon/MPS):** the comfortable path from
  Chapter 5 onward, turning training runs that take minutes on a GPU
  into ones that take hours on CPU. `bitsandbytes` (used for 4-/8-bit
  QLoRA fine-tuning) installs on Linux+NVIDIA, but no chapter in this
  book actually loads a quantized model — every chapter fine-tunes with
  full-precision LoRA, the path Chapter 5 walks you through, so a GPU
  here just makes that same LoRA fine-tune faster, not a different
  technique.
- **CPU only:** still possible for the earliest chapters (loading a
  model, baseline prompting, tokenization) and for fine-tuning a very
  small model, but training runs will be noticeably slower. Expect to
  reduce dataset size and steps for CPU-only exercises.
- **No cloud account or paid API is required anywhere in this book.**

## 4. A note on data handling

This book's own data (`datasets/sample_training_set/`,
`datasets/full_training_set/`) is public and safe to commit, share, and
publish — that's true throughout this repository. The moment you point
this book's code at your own organisation's reports instead, that
changes:

- Never commit real, confidential reports, extracted text, training
  examples, or model checkpoints trained on them to a public repository.
- If you're experimenting on a shared machine, confirm your
  organisation's data classification policy covers running third-party
  Python packages (model downloads, tokenizers) against confidential
  well data.
- Add your own archive's path to `.gitignore` before dropping any
  confidential reports into a local `datasets/` folder for testing.
- Before fine-tuning on your own organisation's data, confirm you have
  the right to use it for this purpose — that determination is outside
  the scope of this book.

## 5. Troubleshooting

[Part 0, Section 0.11](../chapters/chapter_00.qmd) covers the common
setup errors (Python not found, virtual environment not active, and so
on). A few more specific to rendering the book or running heavier
fine-tuning packages:

| Symptom | Likely cause |
|---|---|
| `quarto render` fails on a code cell | Activate `.venv` before rendering — Quarto uses whichever Python is on `PATH`. Confirm with `which python` and `python -c "import transformers"`. |
| `ModuleNotFoundError: peft` or `trl` (Chapter 5+) | Re-run `pip install -r requirements.txt`; these are heavier dependencies that pull in `torch` and sometimes need a platform-specific `torch` install first. |
| `bitsandbytes` fails to import | It's Linux + NVIDIA GPU only (see `requirements.txt`). On macOS or CPU-only Linux, skip 4-/8-bit quantized fine-tuning and use full-precision LoRA instead. |
| Training is extremely slow | Confirm a GPU is actually being used (`torch.cuda.is_available()` or `torch.backends.mps.is_available()`); on CPU-only hardware, reduce dataset size and steps as suggested in the relevant chapter. |
